opportunities.theorem: For every finite field k=F_q and countable group H with a,b in k[H], ab=1, ba!=1, put G=H*Z, X=k^G, p=1-ba, K=T_p X, m=|supp(p) supp(p)^(-1)|+1. There is a standard p.m.p. G-system R with K^m isomorphic to X times R and X isomorphic to X^n times R^(n-1) for every n>=1. The weak Pinsker entropy of X is infinite.
assumptions: An actual one-sided inverse pair is supplied; no concrete witness is constructed or verified here
The group is enlarged to the free product H*Z
Left shift and right convolution T_c x(h)=sum_s c_s x(hs)
opportunities.mechanism: Malnormality makes every nonidentity group element move infinitely many independent nonzero Haar blocks. The resulting free seed colors overlapping finite input windows. A scalar-normalized locally finite toggle operator is a continuous right inverse for each seed, so the full compact-group fiber splits with product Haar measure.
opportunities.stronger_lemma: For any 0!=c in F_q[H], the image T_c(F_q^(H*Z)) is essentially free and a finite power splits off the full F_q Bernoulli shift, independently of idempotence or a one-sided inverse witness.
opportunities.historical_importance: Connects a direct finiteness witness to arbitrarily large exact direct Bernoulli factors. This strengthens the conditional entropy consequence without claiming unequal-entropy Bernoulli conjugacy.
opportunities.load_bearing_missing_input_for_concrete_: Independent verification of a concrete group-ring witness
early_falsification_tests: Find a nonidentity g fixing infinitely many H-cosets in H*Z
Find a nonzero scalar row whose Haar evaluation is nonuniform
Find two same-color support windows that intersect
Break F_eta L_eta=I, joint Borel measurability, or the compact-group product-Haar identity
compatibility_obligations_checked: One-sided inverse survives the injective free-product embedding
The seed free part is invariant and conull
The scalar pivot is inverted for arbitrary finite fields
The displayed infinite right-inverse sum is coordinatewise finite
The residual is a standard Borel p.m.p. action
The Bernoulli output is independent of the entire residual
The same residual works for all n

rejected_unqualified_claims.claim: Every nonzero defect over a countable group with torsion is essentially free and splits a Bernoulli factor from some finite power
rejected_unqualified_claims.counterexample: Given a witness over H, adjoin a nontrivial finite central group N of order invertible in k. With central averaging idempotent e_N, take a'=(1-e_N)+a e_N and b'=(1-e_N)+b e_N. Their defect is (1-ba)e_N!=0 and N acts trivially on its entire image. No finite power can measure-preservingly factor onto k^(H times N).

rejected_unqualified_claims.claim: Mixing alone gives essential freeness even for finite-order elements
rejected_unqualified_claims.counterexample: The image of 1+u+u^2 in F_2[C_3 times Z] is a nonzero mixing factor with pointwise C_3 kernel.

rejected_unqualified_claims.claim: Seward's theorem is needed to infer infinite weak Pinsker entropy from X isomorphic to X^n times R^(n-1)
rejected_unqualified_claims.reason: X^n itself has base entropy n log q, which is already unbounded. Seward adds each prescribed finite entropy.
